clue.text: I'm employed in the theatre

parts.note: the theatre sounds like a stage, but it is the operating theatre, and the speaker is a surgeon's cutting tool

explanation.walkthrough: An operating theatre is where surgery is done; the instrument speaks for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small sharp knife is the tool used during operations in a hospital theatre.

clue.text: Attempt to work out two thirds of the county

indicators.note: only the first four of the county's six letters are kept, so the final third is dropped

parts.note: Sussex is a county in southern England

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to understand most of a county.
explanation.walkthrough: SUSSEX is a county on England's south coast; drop its last third (EX) to leave SUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss something out is informal British slang for investigating it until you understand it.

clue.text: ''Open" to be broadcast at beginning of year

parts.note: a programme on air is being broadcast

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word year

explanation.surface: Something called Open is due to go on air at the start of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room is open and spacious, letting light and breeze through.

clue.text: Writer's sign on a figure

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tag is a label or sign
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author puts a signature on a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Writer's' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Permits, say, for old Latvians

indicators.note: signals that the word is spoken, so its sound counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: lets means allows or permits

explanation.surface: Travel permits are issued to Latvians of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: The Letts were a Baltic people, the ancestors of modern Latvians.

clue.text: Clumsy's cowboy's endless energy

indicators.note: the last letter of the cowboy word is cut off

parts.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A cowboy's tireless vigour is awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Clumsy is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche means socially awkward or lacking grace, a synonym of clumsy.

clue.text: Damage mat and mostly ruin the hall

indicators.note: damaging the letters knocks them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: keeps all but the last letter of ruin

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks a doormat and nearly destroys the entrance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' gives RUI; with MAT that makes MATRUI, rearranged by 'Damage'.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is a large open entrance hall or central court in a building.

clue.text: Back down a mine, covered in copper and dead

indicators.note: the copper symbol wraps around the next pieces

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a pit is a coal mine
the late person means one who has died

explanation.surface: Down a mine, someone is found encased in copper and lifeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back down' looks like a direction into the mine but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To back down is to give in or surrender, which is what capitulating means.

clue.text: Wine maker in presbyter headgear, we hear

indicators.note: says the phrase is spoken aloud and only its sound is used

parts.note: a presbyter is a church elder, and a beret is a soft cap

explanation.surface: A church official in a hat makes wine.
explanation.walkthrough: ELDER BERET said aloud sounds like the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderberries are fermented to make a traditional home-made country wine.

clue.text: Force rents review? Good thought! Ought not to be

indicators.note: the letters of rents are looked over again and re-ordered
the word Ought is removed from thought

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A housing reformer wants rents examined, though the idea should never happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review?' turns RENTS into STREN; 'Ought not to be' strips OUGHT from THOUGHT to leave TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength is power or force, the capacity to exert pressure.

clue.text: Complained: "It's held with insufficient parking"

indicators.note: short of something, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: something held tightly is gripped
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a car park has too few spaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only links; GRIPPED loses one P.
explanation.definitionFit: To gripe is informal for grumbling, so griped means complained.

clue.text: Religious type surrounded by drinks goes off

indicators.note: the religious type sits inside the drinks

parts.note: ales are beers
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theology degree

explanation.surface: A cleric stands among pints and walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg that addles goes rotten, the same as going off.

clue.text: Reused stamps reissued? Apparently all right!

indicators.note: the letters are issued again in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stamps used twice are put back in circulation and seem fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that passed muster was judged acceptable on inspection, so it seemed satisfactory.

clue.text: Cover the freedom of movement that gives set instructions

parts.note: to screen is to shield or cover
play is looseness that allows movement, as in a rope

explanation.surface: Something hides the free motion that tells a set what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A film script tells actors and crew on set what to say and do.

clue.text: Unable to get through, but ample basis for change

indicators.note: the letters are to be changed into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone can't get past, yet there is plenty of ground for reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impassable cannot be crossed or travelled through.

clue.text: Inferior fish around lake? Can't it be cured?

parts.note: common can mean low-class or inferior

indicators.note: the fish wraps around the letter for lake

parts.note: cod is a sea fish
L is a map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A cheap fish caught by a lake prompts the question of a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: There famously is no cure for this everyday virus, hence the question.
explanation.definitionFit: This viral infection of the nose and throat has no cure, as the saying goes.

clue.text: Wince to see boxing in church

indicators.note: the boxing piece goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the ring is the arena for boxing

explanation.surface: It's painful to watch a prizefight held in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe is to flinch or shrink back, as in a wince.

clue.text: Resting place for the ball? It's unbelievable

definitions.meaning: in golf, the spot where a ball comes to rest
a falsehood is something not to be believed

explanation.definitionFit: A golf ball's lie is where it settles; a falsehood is a lie.

clue.text: Made to take in organised group by agent

parts.note: a force is a body of organised people, such as police
a fed is an American federal agent

explanation.surface: A recruit is compelled to join a unit by an official.
explanation.definitionFit: Force-fed means made to swallow food against one's will.

clue.text: Age plays a part in the race

indicators.note: the answer forms part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Age is a factor in the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, an age.

clue.text: The arm produces awkward delivery after big hit

indicators.note: the delivery piece comes after the hit piece

parts.note: in cricket, six runs are scored for a hit over the boundary
in cricket, a shooter is a ball that skids low after bouncing

explanation.surface: A cricketer's throwing arm sends down a tricky ball after a huge stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides 'arm' as a weapon; a six-shooter is a revolver.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-shooter is a revolver, a firearm, so arm in its weapon sense.

clue.text: Neckwear with colour in layers

parts.note: a tie is worn round the neck
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A colourful necktie is worn with several layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiered is arranged in rows or levels, one above another.

clue.text: Repair to the clutch here

parts.note: repair means go back to, and a clutch is a set of eggs, not a car part

explanation.walkthrough: The car-mechanic reading of 'Repair' and 'clutch' misleads; a bird returns to its eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird returns to its brood of eggs at the site where it built its home.

clue.text: Tree span supporting line

indicators.note: in a down clue, the span sits below and holds up the line letter

parts.note: an arch spans a gap

explanation.surface: A tree stretches over a row of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a deciduous conifer, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Technical language has no tips for the vessel

indicators.note: the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: jargon is specialist language

explanation.surface: Technical terms lacking advice, aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship sailed by Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.

clue.text: Second retreat?

definitions.meaning: to second a proposal is to support it

explanation.definitionFit: Back can mean support a motion or move backwards away from something.

clue.text: One defending the dodgy boiler

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man protecting a faulty boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: A libero, or sweeper, is a football defender behind the back line.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a libero is a free defender who sweeps behind the back line.

clue.text: Standard document from holder of chair or graduate

parts.note: a professor holds a university chair
taken as written
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate degree

explanation.surface: A form arrives from a professor or a postgraduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma is a standard printed template or form.

clue.text: Gives up the financial returns

explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way, and yields are the returns produced by investments.

clue.text: Fishy character cheated at the plant

parts.note: to be had is to be tricked
dock is a weed

explanation.surface: A dodgy person was swindled at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' suggests suspicious, but it means a fish; 'plant' means a weed, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The haddock is an edible sea fish, so a fishy creature.
